summary: Specifies a SIP completion of calls feature that notifies the caller of a failed call when the callee becomes available. The basic solution without queuing uses the dialog event package of RFC 4235, described as Automatic Redial in RFC 5359.

eli5.summary: You call a friend and they are busy. The phone tells you when they are free, so you can try again.

subtitle: How a SIP caller who hit a busy or unanswered callee gets recalled automatically when the callee becomes available.

tldr.problem: When a SIP call fails because the callee is busy, does not answer or is not registered, the caller has to keep guessing when to try again.
tldr.mechanism: The caller's agent subscribes to a call-completion event package at the callee's monitor, which queues the request and sends a NOTIFY with cc-state ready when the callee is available, so a CC call can be placed.
tldr.outcome: SIP gets a queue-based completion of calls service that works end to end between the two user agents, is designed to interoperate with SS7 services, and has a simple Automatic Redial approach as a fallback.

today: RFC 6910 is a Proposed Standard from April 2013. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its simple fallback, Automatic Redial, is described in RFC 5359.

sections.title: What Completion of Calls Does
sections.content:
The Completion of Calls (CC) feature lets the caller of a failed call have the call completed without guessing when the callee becomes available. The callee is monitored. When it is free, it gets a time frame to start a call itself; if it does not, the caller is recalled. When the caller accepts the recall, a CC call to the callee starts automatically. If several callers asked, they are recalled in a predefined order, usually the order of their requests.

Three variants are defined, selected by the reason for failure:

  • CCBS (busy subscriber): the caller is recalled after the callee is no longer busy.
  • CCNR (no reply): the caller is recalled after the callee has completed a new call.
  • CCNL (not logged in): the caller is recalled after the callee has registered again.

The RFC notes that a failed call may look successful to SIP. A call that reaches voicemail gets a 200 response, yet the caller may consider it failed, so CC can be invoked even then.
sections.eli5: If your friend is busy, does not pick up, or has their phone off, you can ask the phone system to call you back when they are ready.

sections.title: Architecture: Caller's Agent and Callee's Monitor
sections.content:
The architecture adds two logical components. A caller's agent (CC agent) is attached to the caller's user agent. A callee's monitor (CC monitor) is attached to the callee's user agent. Each can be built into the user agent, be a separate end system, be a centralized application server or be provided by home proxies. The two functions are independent even though a user agent is expected to have both.

Only the two end sides need to support CC. Intermediate proxies and B2BUAs only have to pass the usual SIP messages through, whereas in the PSTN intermediate nodes such as media gateway controllers must also implement CC. This is one of the differences from SS7 that the RFC lists. Another is that SIP forking makes success and failure ambiguous, so the caller's agent must record successful calls as well as unsuccessful ones.

Most of the interaction between the agent or monitor and their users, and the policy by which a monitor arbitrates between several requests, is out of scope. Appendices A and B sketch simple examples that use only standard SIP features and are described as suitable only as a learning aid because their performance is poor.
sections.eli5: There are two helpers. One works for the person calling and asks to be called back. The other works for the person being called and keeps the waiting list.

sections.title: The Call Completion Procedure
sections.content:
The callee's monitor inserts a Call-Info header field with purpose=call-completion into non-100 provisional or final responses to the original INVITE. It carries the monitor's URI and an m parameter for the mode: m=BS for busy, m=NR for no response and m=NL for non-registered. The caller's agent then sends SUBSCRIBE requests for the call-completion event package, as defined in RFC 6665, to all known monitor URIs and, if forking is unclear, the original request-URI.

The monitor answers with a NOTIFY carrying cc-state: queued. When the callee is available and this request is selected, a NOTIFY with cc-state: ready goes out. The caller's agent checks that the caller is available, for example by calling the caller's UA, and has the UA send a new INVITE for the CC call, marked with the m URI parameter so it gets precedence.

If the caller is not available at the recall, the agent sends a PUBLISH with presence state "closed" to suspend the request, and later a PUBLISH with "open" to resume it. Suspending lets the monitor move on to the next request in the queue.

When a CC call fails, the retain option decides what happens. A monitor that supports the retain option sends a cc-service-retention line, and the request keeps its queue position. Without it, a failed CC call deletes the request and the subscription ends, and the agent may subscribe again.
sections.eli5: You get a ticket and wait. When it is your turn, your phone tells you. If you cannot talk right now, you say "skip me for now" and the next person goes, then you can say "I am back".

sections.title: The CC Queue Model
sections.content:
A callee's monitor manages CC for a single URI, which may be a published address of record or as narrow as one UA's contact URI. It holds a set of CC entities (CCEs), one for each CC request, meaning each incoming CC subscription. Each CCE has two kinds of state.

  • An availability state, "available" or "unavailable", taken from the caller's presence status ("open" or "closed") set through PUBLISH requests as in RFC 3903.
  • A recall state, "queued" or "ready", visible through the subscription.

A new CCE starts as available and queued. A request is eligible for recall only when its availability state is "available" and its m value also indicates an available state, and the monitor MUST NOT select any other. Within that limit, local policy decides, and often the longest-waiting entry is picked. Selection changes the recall state from queued to ready and triggers a notification. If the selected subscriber then suspends, the recall state goes back to queued and another entry may be chosen.
sections.eli5: The waiting list has a name and a sign saying "here" or "away" for each person. Only people marked "here" can be called next, and usually the one who waited longest goes first.

sections.title: Timers and Monitor Behavior
sections.content:
On sending the ready notification, the callee's monitor MUST start a recall timer. A value between 10 and 20 seconds is RECOMMENDED, matching ETSI and ITU-T recommendations for CC services. When the CC call arrives, the timer MUST be stopped. If it expires first, the monitor SHOULD stop the recall and set the state back to "queued" when it supports the retain option, or terminate the subscription when it does not.

If the CC call succeeds, the monitor MUST terminate the subscription and remove the presence state used for suspend and resume. A suspension via PUBLISH makes the monitor stop the recall timer, set the request to "queued" and try another request.

The default subscription duration is 3600 seconds, the highest service duration timer value recommended in the ETSI and ITU-T documents, and subscribers and notifiers are RECOMMENDED to use at least that. A notifier whose queue is full MUST reply 480 Temporarily Unavailable, and one that can never provide CC MUST reply 403 Forbidden. Redundant forks of the same SUBSCRIBE (same Call-Id) are rejected with 482 Merged Request except for one.
sections.eli5: When it is your turn the phone only waits a short while, between 10 and 20 seconds, for you to answer. If you do not, you go back in line.

sections.title: The call-completion Event Package and Body
sections.content:
Section 9 defines the call-completion event package, in line with RFC 6665, with the media type application/call-completion. NOTIFY requests MUST carry a body describing the CC state. The body is a set of header-like lines: names are case-insensitive, lines can be continued, unknown names are ignored, and each defined line occurs at most once.

  • cc-state: "queued" or "ready". It MUST be present unless the expiration time in the NOTIFY is zero.
  • cc-service-retention: the value "true" says the retain option is supported.
  • cc-URI: a URI the agent SHOULD use as the request-URI of the CC recall INVITE and of the suspend/resume PUBLISH. It SHOULD be globally routable and unique to the CCE.

To limit notification load, a notifier SHOULD NOT generate more than three notifications for one subscription in any ten-second interval, and SHOULD NOT send a change to "ready" as the third one, so it can still promptly send a change back to "queued".
sections.eli5: The messages are short notes with labels like "status: ready" and "call this number". That is all the agent needs to know.

sections.title: Privacy and Abuse Concerns
sections.content:
CC lets the caller's agent learn some status information about the callee, which intrinsically diminishes the callee's privacy. The RFC says disclosure must be limited overall and per caller. A caller who is not permitted to call the callee should not be able to subscribe. A sensible approach is to let any caller subscribe but not for too long, too often, or in patterns that hide the subscription from the callee.

Legitimate use looks stereotyped: a call should arrive promptly after selection, subscriptions should not stay suspended longer than a call to a third party, they should start soon after a failed call, and most of the time a callee should have no queued subscriptions. Violations should be detected by the monitor and reported as possible privacy violations.

The RFC also warns CC could make spam over Internet telephony more effective, since CC calls are more likely to reach callees. To prevent denial of service and suspending other people's entries, it recommends authenticating request originators with the SIP Identity mechanism of RFC 4474, or P-Asserted-Identity from RFC 3325 inside a trusted domain or federation.
sections.eli5: If anyone could join the waiting list, they could learn when you are busy or free. So the system should limit how long and how often people can ask, and check who they really are.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The RFC registers several things.

  • The SIP event package call-completion (not a template package).
  • The media type application/call-completion, intended usage LIMITED USE, with UTF-8 lines ended by CRLF.
  • A new SIP/SIPS URI parameter m, which marks an INVITE as a CC call or a SUBSCRIBE as for the call-completion package.
  • A new purpose value call-completion for the Call-Info header field.
  • An m header parameter for Call-Info, with predefined values BS, NR and NL.
sections.eli5: New names and labels get written in the official list so nobody else uses them for something different.
